decision.identity_checks: Every compared process returned identical input/rejection/receipt identities; all peak-RSS guards passed.
decision.outcome: verified improvement for complete verification on the measured synthetic contracts
decision.primary_boundary: Complete verify, including deterministic in-process fixture execution, protocol rejection checks and durable receipt writes.
decision.primary_threshold: At least 15% lower ratio-of-arm-median elapsed time in both widths and both profiles.
decision.qualification: Admission-only timings are mixed and noisy; no uniform admission-only speedup is established. No provider, container or hosted-CI latency claim.
retained: Reuse compiled schemas within each immutable contract admission.
Admit the immutable contract once in verify, through validate_candidate, before computing the same receipt digest.

experiments.finding: Wide release admission missed the 15% threshold (9.93% lower arm median); small loops of about 10–25 ms had large scheduling variability.

build_options.debug: opt-level=0, debug assertions enabled; sha2 package uses repository opt-level=3
build_options.release: opt-level=3, LTO off; no profile changes between arms

limitations: Synthetic bounded contracts; fixture verification uses an in-process runner and performs real durable receipt writes.
The timed admission boundary excludes input construction and process startup; process_ns records complete probe elapsed time.
No claim about provider latency, Docker execution or hosted CI duration.

experiments.finding: Combined schema reuse and removal of two repeated frozen-contract admissions lowered complete-verification arm medians by 26.43–29.82%. Longer loops were declared before this run to reduce short-sample variability.

limitations: Synthetic bounded contracts; fixture verification uses an in-process runner and performs real durable receipt writes.

No claim about provider latency, Docker execution or hosted CI duration.
